raw_description: The remote SSH server is running a version of OpenSSH that is affected by multiple vulnerabilities. Detected version: OpenSSH 7.4.
note: 7.4 falls inside the synthetic affected range 7.0-7.9 and evidence directly supports the version.

raw_description: The remote SSH server may be running an outdated OpenSSH version with known issues.
note: 9.3 is well outside the affected range 7.0-7.9 -- classic scanner over-report.

raw_description: Apache HTTP Server is vulnerable to a path traversal and remote code execution issue.
evidence: Server header: Apache/2.4.49 (Unix), confirmed via curl ../../../../etc/passwd returned file contents
note: Exact affected version AND direct exploitation evidence in the finding.

raw_description: Apache HTTP Server may be vulnerable to path traversal.
note: 2.4.51 is outside the narrow affected range (only 2.4.49) -- a very commonly misreported case.

raw_description: The remote service supports TLS 1.0, which is deprecated.
evidence: nmap ssl-enum-ciphers shows TLSv1.0 listed alongside TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3; TLSv1.2 negotiated by default in handshake test
note: Version is in range, but the false-positive note applies: TLS1.0 is merely offered, not necessarily negotiable/exploitable -- evidence is ambiguous, a human should confirm whether TLS1.0 can actually be forced.

raw_description: MySQL service may be using default or weak credentials.
evidence: Port 3306 open, MySQL banner detected. No login attempt recorded.
note: Config-class issue, version irrelevant, but no direct evidence of a successful login -- cannot confirm from this alone.

raw_description: MySQL service is using default credentials.
evidence: Successful login recorded using root/root with no password prompt bypass required.
note: Direct login evidence present -- this one should be confirmed despite being config-class/version-independent.

raw_description: vsftpd version detected matches a known backdoored release.
note: Exact match to the single known-bad release.

raw_description: vsftpd service detected, flagged for backdoor check.
note: Different version entirely -- scanner flagged the service name/plugin generically, not the specific vulnerable release.

raw_description: Redis server may allow unauthenticated access.
evidence: Port 6379 open. Redis banner detected. Direct PING command returned PONG with no AUTH required.
note: Direct evidence unauthenticated access actually works -- the challenging case: config-class issue where evidence quality (not version) is what separates Confirmed from Needs Verification (contrast with case-06).

raw_description: The remote SSH server is running a version of OpenSSH that is affected.
note: First sighting of this host+plugin pair -- sets up case-12 to test memory/dedupe.

raw_description: The remote SSH server is running a version of OpenSSH that is affected.
note: Exact duplicate of case-11 (same host+plugin, as a real scan sometimes reports the same finding twice via different plugin checks). Tests that memory/dedupe actually gets exercised in scored eval, not just claimed in the changelog.

raw_description: Elasticsearch instance may expose indices without authentication.
note: Plugin not present in vuln_db.json -- tests the tool-lookup-miss path (system correctly declines to guess rather than defaulting to Confirmed or False Positive).

raw_description: SSH version could not be reliably determined by the scanner.
evidence: Banner grab returned no version string.
note: Unparseable version string -- tests the version-parse-failure path (must not silently default to Confirmed or False Positive).

raw_description: The remote SSH server is running OpenSSH 7.0.
note: Exact lower-boundary version (range is 7.0-7.9 inclusive) -- tests that range comparison is inclusive at the boundary, not off-by-one.

evidence: TLSv1.2 is negotiated by default in a normal handshake, but a forced downgrade attack to TLSv1.0 succeeded, allowing plaintext recovery of a session cookie.
note: ADVERSARIAL CASE -- deliberately designed to try to break the evidence-contradiction heuristic. The evidence contains the literal phrase 'negotiated by default' (which case-05's fix treats as a signal the vuln ISN'T active) but the same sentence goes on to describe a real, successful downgrade attack. A superficial keyword match will likely misclassify this as 'Needs Verification' when it should be 'Confirmed' -- this is expected to reveal a genuine limitation of pattern-based evidence checking, not a bug to silently fix before running the eval.
